title: Toner stock exists but cannot be found
source_story: User-provided fictional owner stories in this conversation; opening narrative below is a faithful condensed adaptation, not a verbatim transcript.
business_context: Printer rental and consumables provider; approximately 650 managed devices.
owner_narrative: The spreadsheet says five cartridges, but some are in vans, reserved or already delivered. Customers identify a printer by its location and sometimes photograph the wrong one. Leaving spare toner helped some sites but caused others to stockpile it.

diagnostic_interview.question: Is the warning an empty cartridge?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Some callers report the first low-toner warning while a spare is already on-site.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: If physical counts are accurate but consumption exceeds replenishment lead time, reorder policy rather than data capture is the main issue.

diagnostic_interview.question: What does stock count include?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Reservations and van stock are mixed with warehouse stock.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

diagnostic_interview.question: How is compatibility verified?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Staff use memory or a customer photograph.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

diagnostic_interview.question: Are deliveries recorded immediately?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Often at the end of the week.
diagnostic_interview.diagnostic_value: Stock freshness is a root issue.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

evidence.description: A simulated stock audit separates warehouse, reserved and van quantities.
A simulated delivery receipt is absent from the stock sheet.
A simulated customer check finds two unopened spares.

diagnoses.hypothesis: Missing location and reservation accounting combines with unreliable device and customer-stock identification.
diagnoses.counterhypothesis: If physical counts are accurate but consumption exceeds replenishment lead time, reorder policy rather than data capture is the main issue.
diagnoses.confidence_policy: Qualitative case-world support only; requires fresh customer evidence before reuse.

interventions.process_first: Count high-use stock; assign device IDs; log transfers at handover; ask about usable on-site spare stock before urgent delivery.
interventions.deterministic_and_assisted_automation: Maintain a location ledger and compatibility table; reserve stock atomically; suggest replenishment for human approval until counts are reliable.
interventions.rejected_default: Do not replace the whole service platform or deploy autonomous agents solely because the owner reports inefficiency.
interventions.selection_basis: Choose the least complex intervention addressing the supported handoff failure; compare added administration and integration burden.

requirements.statement: Available stock equals physical quantity minus valid reservations at that location.
requirements.rationale: Missing location and reservation accounting combines with unreliable device and customer-stock identification.

requirements.statement: An incompatible or uncertain SKU blocks picking.
requirements.rationale: Missing location and reservation accounting combines with unreliable device and customer-stock identification.

requirements.statement: A retry with the same movement ID cannot decrement twice.
requirements.rationale: Missing location and reservation accounting combines with unreliable device and customer-stock identification.

requirements.statement: Reorder proposals include lead time and confidence in counts.
requirements.rationale: Missing location and reservation accounting combines with unreliable device and customer-stock identification.

acceptance_tests.scenario_and_expected_result: Two reservations cannot consume the same final cartridge.
A van-to-site delivery changes both locations once.
An unknown model requires verification before fulfillment.

capability_boundary.proposed_extension: Inventory ledger, asset compatibility and replenishment logic are proposed extensions.
capability_boundary.pricing: No price assigned; current rate card must not be extended by analogy.

evaluation.primary_metric_definition: Emergency toner trips / toner fulfillments; also track stock accuracy and stockout days to avoid improving trips by overstocking.
measurement_cautions: Use a stable denominator and comparable operating periods.
Record missingness and changed case mix.
Do not infer staff reductions from reclaimed task minutes.

implementation.baseline: Collect at least one representative operating cycle before rollout; for monthly billing or maintenance include the relevant full cycle. Extend sampling when volumes or seasonality make the sample unrepresentative.
implementation.scope: Start with one consenting customer group and the staff who own its handoffs; include a normal case and each listed exception.
sequence: Reconcile identities and existing obligations with the process owner.
Run the proposed rules in shadow mode; record disagreements and missed exceptions.
Approve a bounded live pilot only after requirements and exceptions have named owners.
Review outcome metrics, added administrative work and failure logs before expanding.
implementation.simulated_resolution: In this fictional case, MILO introduced the process change: Count high-use stock; assign device IDs; log transfers at handover; ask about usable on-site spare stock before urgent delivery. The team adopted the proposed workflow for the pilot scope. Routine coordination became explicit; unresolved exceptions continued to require a person.
implementation.simulated_lesson: If physical counts are accurate but consumption exceeds replenishment lead time, reorder policy rather than data capture is the main issue.
implementation.rollback: Pause automated writes and notifications, retain the event log, export outstanding work and return to a named manual coordinator. Reconcile queued events before resuming to avoid duplicate actions.
implementation.go_no_go: Process owner reviews coverage of acceptance cases, unresolved critical failures, metric direction and staff workload. No fixed performance threshold is claimed without customer agreement.

open_questions: OEM compatibility, supplier lead times and actual usage distributions are not supplied.

transfer_rules.do_not_assume: If physical counts are accurate but consumption exceeds replenishment lead time, reorder policy rather than data capture is the main issue.
